instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Run PubMed Title-field search for the exact phrase
criteria.description: Perform the PubMed query using the Title field (not an all-fields search) for the phrase "large language model". Full credit if the final query clearly targets Title (e.g., [Title] or [ti]) and uses the specified phrase. Partial credit if the phrase is used but field restriction is unclear/incorrect. Full credit if PubMed is inaccessible (e.g., captcha/outage) but the agent clearly attempts the correct Title-field query and reports the blocker; no credit if the search is not on PubMed or the agent makes no reasonable attempt.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest) shows a PubMed bot-check/reCAPTCHA overlay (“Select all images… VERIFY”) with faint background text referencing pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov. Screenshot 1 shows “403 Forbidden.” Action history shows the agent visited https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22large%20language%20model%22%5BTitle%5D which is a Title-field query for the exact phrase.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Although the screenshots do not display the query string on-page, the action history confirms a correct Title-field URL query attempt. The latest screenshot confirms an uncontrollable access blocker (CAPTCHA) preventing verification within the UI. No contradiction or fabrication by the agent; full credit is appropriate under blocker rules.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a Google reCAPTCHA-style image selection widget overlay. Text at top reads: “Select all images with a fire hydrant” and “Click verify once there are none left.” A 3x3 image grid is visible with a blue “VERIFY” button. Behind the overlay, faint page text appears: “Checking your br…” and “pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov …”. No PubMed search box, no query string, and no visible term like “large language model” or “[Title]” are shown.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot does not provide visible evidence that a PubMed Title-field search for the exact phrase was executed. It does, however, confirm an access blocker (CAPTCHA/bot check) on pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, which could prevent performing the search. The agent’s predicted output (stating a reCAPTCHA block) is consistent with what is shown, but the actual Title-field query is not visible in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent action history suggests a URL with %22large%20language%20model%22%5BTitle%5D, but the screenshot itself does not display that query or any PubMed results page—only the CAPTCHA prompt. No contradiction, just lack of on-screen confirmation of the query.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a mostly blank white page with the text “403 Forbidden” in the top-left corner. No PubMed search box, query text, or any indication of a Title-field search (e.g., [Title], [ti]) is visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot provides no visual evidence that a PubMed Title-field search for the exact phrase “large language model” was executed. It only shows an access error (403). The agent’s predicted output mentions a reCAPTCHA/bot-check page, but the screenshot shows a 403 error, not a CAPTCHA; however, both indicate PubMed is inaccessible, which could prevent completing the search.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent predicted output claims a reCAPTCHA challenge (“Checking your browser…”, reCAPTCHA iframe, VERIFY button). The screenshot instead shows only “403 Forbidden” and no CAPTCHA elements. No visible evidence of the attempted Title-field query appears on-screen.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Latest DOM state is DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1, showing URL `https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22large%20language%20model%22%5BTitle%5D` and a reCAPTCHA interstitial (“Checking your browser - reCAPTCHA”). This explicitly includes the exact phrase and the `[Title]` field restriction in the query URL.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The Title-field search was correctly constructed and attempted on PubMed, and the DOM explicitly supports the `[Title]` restriction and phrase. Blocker does not negate the correct query attempt. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows URL `https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22large%20language%20model%22%5BTitle%5D` and page title `Checking your browser - reCAPTCHA` with visible text `Checking your browser before accessing pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov ...`.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The loaded PubMed URL explicitly contains the exact quoted phrase and Title-field restriction: `%22large%20language%20model%22` (= "large language model") and `%5BTitle%5D` (= [Title]), which is a correct attempt to run the required Title-field search on PubMed.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None for the query construction itself. However, the DOM does not show actual PubMed results due to the reCAPTCHA interstitial.

criteria.description: Apply BOTH PubMed filters exactly as specified: (1) Article type = Review (not Systematic Review unless the returned items are also classified as Review), and (2) Publication date = Past 5 years using PubMed's relative filter. Full credit if both filters are visibly applied OR if the agent clearly indicates both were selected/applied but UI evidence is unavailable due to platform limitations. Partial credit if only one filter is applied, or if the agent substitutes a manual year range instead of PubMed's Past 5 years filter. Full credit if PubMed prevents applying filters (UI failure/blocking) but the agent reports the issue after a reasonable attempt.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest) shows the reCAPTCHA/bot-check and no PubMed filters UI. Screenshot 1 shows a 403 error page. No evidence of filter controls being reachable.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The screenshots confirm an uncontrollable blocker that prevents applying the Review and Past 5 years filters in the PubMed interface. Per rubric principles, when the platform prevents applying filters, award full credit for this criterion (and downstream dependent criteria).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Only the reCAPTCHA challenge is visible (“Select all images with a fire hydrant… VERIFY”). No PubMed filter sidebar/pills are visible; no labels like “Review” or “Past 5 years” appear anywhere in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: There is no evidence that either required filter (Article type = Review, Publication date = Past 5 years) was applied. The screenshot supports that the page is blocked by CAPTCHA, which would prevent applying filters. The agent’s predicted output claims inability to proceed due to CAPTCHA, which matches the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent did not claim filters were applied; it claimed they could not be applied due to CAPTCHA. Screenshot aligns with that—no filters shown.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Only “403 Forbidden” is visible. There are no filter panels, no “Article type” section, no “Review” filter, and no “Past 5 years” publication date filter visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: No evidence that either required filter (Review article type and Past 5 years) was applied. The page appears blocked by a 403 error, which would prevent interacting with PubMed’s filter UI.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent output states it cannot proceed due to a reCAPTCHA; screenshot shows a 403 Forbidden error page instead. In either case, there is no on-screen confirmation of filters being applied.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Latest DOM state (index 1) is a reCAPTCHA interstitial and contains no PubMed results UI and no filter controls/indicators. Earlier DOM state (index 0) is a 403 page with no filter UI. Thus there is no DOM confirmation that the Review article-type filter or Past 5 years filter were applied.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Although an uncontrollable blocker (reCAPTCHA) is confirmed, the agent’s actions/history show only a direct navigation to the Title-restricted search URL and no attempt that could apply filters (no additional actions, and no filter-related URL parameters like `filter=pubt.review` or `filter=datesearch.y_5`). With the DOM rule, we can award credit for being blocked, but not for successfully applying (or even attempting) both filters. Reduce to 0 because neither filter application nor a concrete attempt is evidenced.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 displays only a reCAPTCHA interstitial: `Checking your browser before accessing pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov ...` and `recaptcha challenge expires in two minutes`. No PubMed filters UI is present in the DOM snapshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: UNKNOWN
There is no DOM evidence that the Review article-type filter and the Past 5 years relative date filter were applied. The page shown is a reCAPTCHA block, preventing access to the PubMed results interface where filters would be selected/verified.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Required filters (Review; Past 5 years) cannot be confirmed as applied; no filter chips/sidebars/indicators are visible because PubMed content is not reached.

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: UNKNOWN
The only provided DOM state is a 403 error page, which contains no evidence that the Title-field search results page loaded or that the required PubMed filters (Article type=Review and Publication date=Past 5 years) were available or applied. Because there is no post-action DOM state for the query URL, filter application cannot be verified.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history indicates a navigation attempt to a Title-restricted query URL, but there is no corresponding DOM state showing the search results page or any applied filters. The agent-predicted output mentions a reCAPTCHA challenge, but that is also not shown in the DOM evidence provided.

criteria.description: Change sorting to PubMed's "Most Recent" (or equivalent casing/label such as “Most recent”) and preserve the displayed order for reporting. Full credit if sorting is visibly set to Most Recent OR if the agent clearly states it set Most Recent but UI evidence is unavailable due to platform limitations. Partial credit if sorting is attempted but not clearly confirmed, or order is not preserved. Full credit if PubMed prevents changing sort (UI failure/blocking) but the agent reports the issue after a reasonable attempt.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest) shows reCAPTCHA/bot-check overlay; no results page or sorting dropdown is visible. Screenshot 1 shows 403 Forbidden.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Sorting cannot be changed/verified due to the confirmed platform-level access blocker. Full credit is warranted under uncontrollable-blocker guidance.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the CAPTCHA overlay and a faint “Checking your br…” page behind it. No PubMed results list and no sort control (e.g., “Sort by: Most Recent”) is visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: No evidence that results were sorted by “Most Recent.” The CAPTCHA/bot check shown would prevent reaching the results page to set sorting. The agent’s predicted output (unable to proceed due to CAPTCHA) is consistent with the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No mismatch: agent states it cannot change sorting; screenshot shows access is blocked and no sorting UI is visible.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows only “403 Forbidden” at top-left. No sorting control (e.g., “Sort by: Most Recent”) is present.

evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent output references a reCAPTCHA blocking progress; screenshot shows 403 Forbidden. No sorting UI is visible to support any claim of changing sort.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Latest DOM state (index 1) is a reCAPTCHA interstitial with no results list and no sort control; earlier state (index 0) is a 403 page. No DOM evidence of 'Most Recent' sorting being set, and no action history indicating a sort change or sort-related URL parameter.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Blocker is confirmed, but there is no evidenced attempt to change sorting (no UI interaction possible shown, no URL parameter for sort, no additional actions). Therefore the criterion is not met/attempted in an evidenced way. Score 0.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 is a 403 page (Title: "403") at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/. No sort control (e.g., "Sort by", "Most Recent") is present in the DOM snapshot.

criteria.criterion: Record first result with all required fields
criteria.description: For the first (top) result in the filtered, Most Recent-sorted list, report: full title, PMID, publication type(s) as displayed/classified, and the complete journal citation exactly (journal name, year/date, volume/issue/pages/eLocation as shown). Full credit if all fields are captured and match the listing. Partial credit if one element is missing or citation is incomplete. If fewer than 1 result exists after applying the required query/filters/sort, full credit if the agent clearly reports that no results are returned (or results are unavailable due to PubMed access issues) and does not fabricate details.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest) shows reCAPTCHA/bot-check; no search results, titles, PMIDs, publication types, or citations visible. Screenshot 1 shows 403 Forbidden.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Because the blocker prevents access to the results list, the agent cannot record the first result’s fields. The agent did not fabricate any record details and correctly reported inability to proceed. Full credit under uncontrollable-blocker rules.

criteria.criterion: Stop after capturing the first three results (stopping condition)
criteria.description: Stop once the specified query, both filters, and Most Recent sorting are applied and the first three results' required fields have been recorded, or once it is confirmed that fewer than three results exist. Full credit if the agent does not continue browsing beyond what is needed. Partial credit if extra unnecessary navigation occurs but does not change results/order. No credit if the agent continues and ends up reporting items from a changed query/filter/sort state or fabricates missing items.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest) indicates the session is halted at the reCAPTCHA step; Screenshot 1 shows 403 Forbidden. No evidence of unnecessary additional navigation beyond the blocker.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent stopped once it encountered the access blocker and did not continue with unnecessary browsing or fabricate results. Given the blocker, this is an appropriate stopping point; keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the session halted at a CAPTCHA (“Select all images with a fire hydrant” and “VERIFY”). No evidence of further navigation or additional pages/results beyond this blocker is visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The stopping condition (stop after applying query+filters+sort and capturing first three results) is not met because the task cannot proceed past the CAPTCHA and no results were captured. However, the agent effectively stops due to the blocker and does not continue browsing or fabricate outputs, which is consistent with the screenshot’s blocked state.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output indicates it cannot proceed and thus cannot capture results; screenshot shows a CAPTCHA that would cause exactly this halt. No discrepancy.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows an immediate access error (“403 Forbidden”) and no evidence of continued navigation, scrolling, or additional pages.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: From the screenshot alone, it appears the process stops at an access-blocked page and does not proceed further. The agent’s predicted output states it cannot proceed due to blocking, which aligns with a stopping condition being met due to inability to access results (though the specific blocker type differs).

dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Although the formal stopping condition (filters + sorting applied + three results recorded) was not reached due to the blocker, the agent appropriately stopped once blocked and did not continue irrelevant navigation. Full credit for this criterion’s intent (no unnecessary extra steps).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 indicates the session is stopped at a reCAPTCHA interstitial (no subsequent DOM states/actions beyond Action 1). There is no evidence of continued navigation within PubMed results.

The agent did not proceed beyond the initial attempted search URL (no extra navigation is evidenced). However, the stopping condition as defined (query + both filters + sorting applied + first three results recorded) is not met/confirmable because the workflow is blocked prior to applying filters/sorting and extracting results.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Only DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 is provided (403 page). There is no DOM evidence of reaching a results page, applying filters/sort, or capturing three results, and no evidence of any additional navigation beyond the initial captured state.

EVIDENCE_STATUS: UNKNOWN
From DOM evidence alone, it cannot be verified that the agent stopped after applying query/filters/sort and recording three results, because none of those steps are visible in the DOM. The single available state indicates an access issue, which would prevent completing the stopping condition in the intended way.
